measurements.note: measured earlier on L40S as part of CUDA Graph capture investigation
hand-written CUDA kernel, no cuBLAS, launched and timed via cudaEvent from a pure C++ host program with no Python involved at all

findings: C++/AVX2 is approximately 24-26x faster than Python/CuPy GPU eager mode (cuBLAS-backed), confirming that removing the interpreter from the hot path yields a large, measured improvement
AVX-512 gave no measurable benefit over AVX2-only on a 20x20 matrix; too small to benefit from wider SIMD registers
a hand-written CUDA kernel (no cuBLAS, no Python, direct cudaEvent-timed launch) still measured ~2.7x SLOWER than plain C++/AVX2 on the CPU, at batch_size=1

this establishes that for this specific operation at this specific scale (single 20x20 matrix, one tick at a time), GPU execution is fundamentally disadvantaged versus CPU SIMD, regardless of how the GPU code is written — kernel launch and PCIe-adjacent overhead dominates even in native C++ CUDA code with no Python or cuBLAS involved

decision for the execution plane: Layer 1 (commutator computation) should run on CPU via AVX2/AVX-512, not GPU, at tick-by-tick granularity; GPU remains the correct choice only for batched/windowed workloads (UMAP/HDBSCAN/clustering re-fits), not the single-tick hot path
not_yet_done: no CPU pinning or real-time kernel tuning applied; current p99 figures (4.95-11.26us across implementations) are not representative of a tuned production deployment

the CUDA kernel here uses a single thread block (20x20=400 threads); no attempt was made to optimize GPU occupancy or try multiple kernel launch strategies (e.g. CUDA Graphs would still fail here due to no cuBLAS involvement, worth testing separately since this kernel avoids the cuBLAS blocker entirely)
